transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-22
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Leah Patel (Redwood Partner Ops); Priya Singh (Aurora Channel Lead), Tom Bennett (Aurora Partner Sales), Elena Marsh (Aurora AE), Derek O'Hara (Solutions Architect)

Summary: quick pipeline triage, identify blockers and owners, agree immediate artifacts to share (playbook, account list, technical deep dive).

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you squeezing this in. we're gonna run about an hour, hour and 15, triage three deals and then sync on the co-sell motion. carlos is with me for the tech bits.
[00:18] Priya Singh: Hi Maya, hi Carlos, thanks. we carved out time because a couple of these opps moved fast and we want to make sure we don't lose momentum.
[00:28] Tom Bennett: yeah, lot of pressure from our AE to get pricing and proof points — they asked about private deployment.
[00:35] Carlos Ruiz: great, i'll jump into the infra gating items when we hit deal two, but prelim: we support hosted + dedicated + private/vpc deployments. our private option is a separate control plane — sometimes i say "redwood private" — transcription will probably call it something else.
[00:50] Elena Marsh: can you give baseline on typical timeline to stand up VPC for a medium deal? last time vendorX said 6-8 weeks and the customer balked.
[01:02] Maya Chen: in our experience it's 2-4 weeks for a standard VPC deploy when customer has cloud infra ready and sso/ids in place. with heavy network constraints or air-gapped it's longer.
[01:16] Derek O'Hara: clarifying — is that for the full managed control plane or for on-prem boxed install?
[01:24] Carlos Ruiz: that's for VPC with our private control plane in their VPC. on-prem/hard air gap is a different path and tends to add 4-6 weeks.
[01:35] Priya Singh: okay good to know. let's jump into deal A — Boreal Health. status: in procurement with an internal security review. risk is SSO and SOC2 evidence.
[01:48] Maya Chen: thanks. Boreal Health, deal size looks promising. status notes from field?
[01:55] Tom Bennett: their info sec team is asking for SOC2 reports, pen test, audit log retention. they also want to limit where data is stored — that was the big ask.
[02:06] Carlos Ruiz: for SOC2 we have whitepaper + certs, we'll share those, and audit logs are available via the console with retention settings. for data residency we can pin regionally in our hosted offering or move to VPC.
[02:22] Elena Marsh: is there a standard redwood doc set we can give procurement vs sending a bunch of ad-hoc slides?
[02:29] Maya Chen: yes i'll share the partner pack + security bundle — it's the one we send to enterprise buyers, includes SOC2, ISO snapshots, pen test summaries.
[02:38] Priya Singh: action: send that to Boreal procurement and loop Derek for any architecture Qs.
[02:45] Derek O'Hara: noted. also want to confirm encryption at rest — customer asked about KMS/HSM support.
[02:52] Carlos Ruiz: yep, we support customer-managed keys through KMS integrations and HSM options for private deployments. will include that in the tech packet.
[03:03] Maya Chen: great. deal A mitigation: send security artifacts and offer a 30-min technical Q/A with Derek.
[03:10] Tom Bennett: that works.
[03:12] 
[03:20] Priya Singh: moving to deal B — Summit Retail (large national chain). this one has the timeline pressure, marketing wants a pilot for June. issue: discount expectations and attribution if we both touch the customer.
[03:33] Maya Chen: what's the expected billing model? are they asking for unit pricing or committed capacity?
[03:39] Tom Bennett: their buying committee likes committed capacity, but they want vendor buddies to share margin. Aurora expects some margin.
[03:46] Leah Patel: on our co-sell economics, we typically have a referral fee vs joint-sell revenue split. referral = X% for introductions, whereas joint-sell requires a contract and revenue share. we'll send a short matrix.
[03:58] Elena Marsh: can you be explicit on who owns the relationship post-sale? our AEs want clarity on support handoff.
[04:05] Maya Chen: generally Aurora would be the primary AE on the account if you're the seller of record; Redwood will provide backend support and an SE-led onboarding. But we can be flexible per account — we should put ownership on a per-opportunity doc so expectations are clear.
[04:18] Priya Singh: agreed. for Summit Retail, can we propose a pilot with a time-limited discount and clear SLA?
[04:26] Carlos Ruiz: SLA and pilot sizing — we should confirm expected RPS and concurrency for the pilot so we can right-size dedicated capacity or batching config.
[04:36] Tom Bennett: they expect 500 concurrent users in peak; not sure how that maps to qps per token.
[04:44] Carlos Ruiz: rough calc, depends on prompt length; we'll need more telemetry, but plan for a dedicated pool for pilot. we'll include an estimate in the follow-up.
[04:55] Maya Chen: action: we'll propose pilot sizing, discount terms, and ownership model for Summit by Friday.
[05:03] 
[05:10] Priya Singh: deal C — Nova Fintech. Opportunity has privacy/legal concerns; they asked about on-prem and auditability. includes RFP with strict data controls.
[05:21] Derek O'Hara: this one's technically complex — RFP wants full audit chain, KMS separation, and proof of model weights not exfiltrated.
[05:30] Carlos Ruiz: model weights exfiltration is more of a threat model conversation; for our private deployments we can restrict outbound network egress and provide audit logs, but we do not ship model weights as a separate deliverable — want to flag that.
[05:44] Elena Marsh: customer asked if Redwood supports model pinning or quantized build variations for FIPS compliance.
[05:51] Carlos Ruiz: we can support model pinning and recommend certain quantization profiles; FIPS-specific builds are possible but require engineering alignment and lead time.
[06:03] Priya Singh: ok that's a potential blocker if RFP requires FIPS out of the box.
[06:08] Maya Chen: for Nova Fintech, mitigation: propose staged approach — run a security sandbox with audit logging, then discuss any FIPS commitments after initial acceptance. legal may need to sign an NDA.
[06:21] Tom Bennett: timeline on that would be critical — RFP due in 3 weeks.
[06:28] Maya Chen: understood. action: schedule NDA/legal intro.
[06:32] 
[06:40] Leah Patel: quick question on lead routing — when Aurora qualifies a lead, how should it be created in Salesforce to ensure proper tracking and attribution?
[06:48] Priya Singh: we currently tag partner leads but sometimes they get reassigned and attribution is lost.
[06:54] Maya Chen: we recommend creating the opportunity with partner as partner record type and include a partner-tracking custom field; we'll share a CRM template in the playbook.
[07:05] Priya Singh: can we get sample email sequences for joint outreach?
[07:09] Leah Patel: yes we'll put an outreach template in the playbook.
[07:14] 
[07:20] Carlos Ruiz: i want to call out a capacity risk — if Summit pilot spikes beyond expectations, we have fallback policies: autoscale to burst or route to hosted variants. But that can change cost materially — we should make cost tradeoffs explicit in the pilot SOW.
[07:34] Tom Bennett: client will push back on variable costs. Aurora is willing to absorb a portion but wants clear caps.
[07:42] Maya Chen: agree — include cost cap clauses and an escalation path.
[07:46] 
[07:52] Priya Singh: any competitors in the deals we should worry about?
[07:56] Elena Marsh: Anthropic showed up in meeting notes for Boreal, Cohere is pushing for Summit.
[08:03] Carlos Ruiz: competitor technical differentiators aside, our ops story and quantization/latency controls are a selling point. also the console observability makes it easier for AEs to show ROI.
[08:16] 
[08:22] Maya Chen: quick housekeeping on co-sell docs — I'll share: co-sell playbook, partner pricing matrix, security bundle, and a short SOW template. Carlos will assemble a 30-min tech deep dive deck focused on VPC, SSO, KMS. Leah will put together the joint outreach templates.
[08:40] Priya Singh: that timeline works — can you send the artifacts by Friday?
[08:44] Maya Chen: yes, aiming for EOD Friday (2026-04-24).
[08:48] Tom Bennett: one more ask — can Redwood provide a short customer-facing case study we can co-brand for the GTM event?
[08:55] Maya Chen: we have a mid-market case study we can adapt; will include in the package and flag legal for co-brand approvals.
[09:05] 
[09:12] Derek O'Hara: i'll follow up with a technical appendix for Nova Fintech's RFP requirements so we can triage must-haves vs nice-to-haves.
[09:18] Carlos Ruiz: perfect — i'll review that and propose mitigations for the RFP controls.
[09:23] 
[09:30] Maya Chen: ok let's recap action items: Maya send playbook + security bundle, Carlos tech deep dive, Priya share account list, Tom confirm GTM event dates, Leah draft outreach. legal intro for Nova Fintech RFP.
[09:46] Priya Singh: thanks all. feel good about next steps.
[09:50] Maya Chen: great, we'll follow up in writing and set the tech deep dive for next week. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
